main_body: Open wooden weapon rack: two side posts, a top beam, a middle rail and a bottom shelf/base, holding four weapons (axes, a sword)
top_band: Light tan band, rows 8-11, on the top beam. The bottom shelf has a matching light tan band, rows 24-27.
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the top beam has a light tan top of about 4 rows (8-11). Below it is a darker brown front face of about 3 rows (12-14), which shades the beam like an eave. The bottom shelf repeats this: a light top at rows 24-27, then a darker front at rows 28-30. The posts and rail sit visibly behind and under the beams. The horizontal beams therefore show real top surfaces, not just a rim line. The front edge is only a modest tone step.

style.evidence: The wood has about 4 steps (light tan, mid tan, brown, dark brown). The outlines are dark brown, which suits the material. The beams and posts are broad, smooth fills with almost no grain, knots or speckle. The weapon heads are simple 2-3 tone blocks. Next to the richly textured stall and well references, the candidate is flatter and thinner, with fewer colours per tile.
